body:
Crypto markets closed November 2 in a defensive crouch, with the total market cap sitting at $2.62T after a 24-hour drawdown of 2.18% and aggregate volume of $60.8B. The mood is cautious rather than panicked — the Fear & Greed index ticked up marginally to 37 from yesterday's 34, still firmly in Fear territory but no longer accelerating to the downside. BTC dominance held at 59.3%, with ETH commanding 10.6%, a ratio that tells you capital is consolidating around the largest names rather than rotating into risk. The session had a grinding, low-conviction feel: sellers in control on most timeframes but no aggressive flush, which in itself warrants watching.

Bitcoin printed $77,450 on the day, down 0.71% over 24 hours and off 3.59% on the week, with hourly pressure running at -0.42% as of print. Volume came in at $21.16B, which is meaningful but not the kind of capitulatory surge that tends to mark durable lows. The $77K handle is the level everyone is watching right now — a clean break below it opens air toward the mid-$70Ks where the next meaningful structural support sits. To the upside, bulls need to reclaim and hold $79K before the picture brightens materially. Until that happens, the path of least resistance remains lower on any macro shock. The Cointelegraph headline noting that Strategy spent triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks rather than BTC is worth flagging — it suggests even the most committed institutional accumulator is redirecting capital at the margin, at least for one cycle.

ETH was the relative standout, scraping out a 24-hour gain of +0.18% to trade at $2,269.96 with $10.11B in volume, though the hourly -0.64% and weekly -2.29% make clear this is resilience by comparison, not strength in absolute terms. UNI was the only other asset in the tracked universe to post a meaningful positive print, up +0.61% on the day and +1.22% on the week at $7.22, likely benefiting from some rotation into DeFi blue chips as the broader market sold off. XRP held its own at $1.25, up +0.14% on the day. The losers were decisive: LINK fell 3.07% to $11.2, AVAX dropped 3.05% to $8.47, SOL slid 1.16% to $93.45 and is now off 8.52% on the week, and DOT sits at $0.937979 — down 9.48% weekly and barely holding psychological support above $0.90. ADA at $0.190376 and BNB at $702.11 both lost ground quietly. The divergence between ETH and SOL is notable: the latter had been eating ETH's lunch on activity metrics for much of 2025, so a week where SOL underperforms by 6 percentage points deserves attention from anyone running relative-value positioning.

The macro backdrop is doing the heavy lifting on the bearish side. The Binance SAFU disclosure — Cointelegraph reporting the exchange tapped half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings and released reserve proof — is the kind of news that rattles confidence even if the mechanics are explainable, arriving as it does alongside a FATF review targeting crypto hubs for money-laundering controls. The Mercado Bitcoin hack, cited by CoinDesk as $40 million drained across 10 chains, is a live reminder that cross-chain infrastructure risk remains acute and will keep institutional risk managers cautious. On the institutional build side, the signals are genuinely constructive at a structural level: Standard Chartered launching tokenized deposits in Hong Kong for corporate clients and NYSE tapping Broadridge to move shareholder voting onto blockchain rails are the kinds of TradFi adoption moves that matter for the 12-month narrative. But markets rarely price 12-month narratives when the Fear index is at 37 and weekly drawdowns are in the high single digits across the board.

Into the next session, the key things to track are BTC's ability to defend $77K on any follow-through selling and whether the ETH-SOL divergence widens or closes — a reversal of that trade would signal momentum rotation back into the high-beta layer. The Mercado Bitcoin situation needs to be monitored for contagion; withdrawals being halted across an exchange of that size can trigger confidence shocks that bleed into broader emerging-market crypto sentiment. The FATF review timing is uncomfortable and could generate regulatory headline risk across Southeast Asian and Latin American markets over the coming week. Watch whether Strategy or other known corporate accumulators return to spot BTC buying in size, as that has historically acted as a short-term sentiment floor. Any macro catalyst that moves rate expectations — a surprise in US labor or inflation data — will be amplified in this thin, fearful tape.
